summary: Routing heuristics weight skew causing incorrect SLA attribution in daily ops reports
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 morning, the daily internal SLA attribution report (generated by reporting-pipeline) shows an unexpected 1.8-2.6% shift of P1/P2 tickets from 'on-time' to 'missed' compared to historical baselines. Impact: Internal SLA dashboards and routing summaries used by SRE and Support Ops are reporting skewed attribution; downstream automation that triggers reminders and escalations has sent spurious follow-ups. Environment: prod | us-east; routing-engine v3.4.1; template-indexer v1.9.4; reporting-pipeline v2.7. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run routing simulation against the last 7 days of ticket traffic using current template weights from template-indexer; 2) Compare SLA attribution results against simulation with re-normalized weights; 3) Query template-indexer API /v1/templates?include_weights=true and inspect weight sums. Observed behavior / logs: - template-indexer API returns template weight lists whose sums are not normalized to 1.0 for ~12% of templates. - routing-engine logs show 'applied_weight' values > 1.0 for some routing decisions (examples at /var/log/routing/2026-03-11.log lines 4821-4860). - reporting-pipeline job rp-job-2026-03-11 produced an aggregation warning: "weight_sum_deviation: true" and emitted a note to the metrics index. Suspected recent change: template-indexer v1.9.4 included a config toggle normalize_weights (default expected true) which appears to have been set to false in the production config bundle.

investigation_notes: Checked config audit log: config-bundle deploy 2026-03-11T02:03 by pipeline 'config-autodeploy' included file prod.yaml with normalize_weights=false. This deviates from expected default.
Grep across template-indexer code: recent commit xyz123 removed a safety normalization step in normalize_weights() but unit tests did not cover edge cases where stored weight_sum != 1.0.
Routing-engine is tolerant and will accept weights as-is; without normalization it amplifies templates that were intended to have fractional influence leading to SLA attribution drift.
Reporting-pipeline currently logs weight_sum_deviation but does not fail job; no alert existed for sustained deviation > 0.5% across >1 hour windows — gap found.

Reindex/backfill approach: Data Eng reprocessed templates and re-ran aggregation. Re-run aggregated metrics matched baseline after normalization. No customer-facing incidents observed; issue limited to internal reports and automation.
Related prs: 1482 (config change), 1490 (template-indexer refactor) - 1490 removed test coverage for zero-sum templates; 1482 flipped flag unintentionally during merging of a staging patch.
resolution: 2026-03-12: Hotfix applied in routing-engine to force normalization at decision time (short-term mitigation).
2026-03-12: Reverted prod config normalize_weights to true (PR revert applied).
2026-03-12: Data Eng completed a reindex and re-run of reporting-pipeline for the affected 72-hour window; SLA attribution metrics returned to expected baselines.
2026-03-13: Added deploy-time schema validation which rejects config bundles where weight_sum deviation > 0.01 for more than 1% of templates.

Follow-ups: 1) Add unit tests to template-indexer to assert normalization invariants (owner: Template Indexer team, due 2026-03-20). 2) Add alert to reporting-pipeline for sustained weight_sum_deviation > 0.5% over 1 hour (owner: Metrics, due 2026-03-18). 3) Update SLA attribution runbook with troubleshooting steps and quick mitigation (owner: Support Ops Docs, due 2026-03-19).
